@graph.name: Mike Ye — Practical M&A Library
@graph.description: Practical M&A judgment, valuation models, due diligence and integration handbooks, transaction lessons, and corporate development frameworks by Mike Ye.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Corporate development
hasDefinedTerm.description: Set the acquisition mandate, prioritize targets, and carry evidence from sourcing through investment approval and operating ownership.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Valuation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Build a defensible valuation range, separate standalone economics from buyer-created value, and connect evidence to price discipline.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Financial modeling
hasDefinedTerm.description: Turn operating assumptions into cash flows, valuation ranges, and acquisition decisions using five downloadable company models.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Comparable-company analysis
hasDefinedTerm.description: Choose comparable public companies, review trading multiples and financial definitions, and support a valuation range.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Deal structure & negotiation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Separate price from funding, compare forms of consideration, and assign unresolved risks before committing to acquisition terms.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Due diligence
hasDefinedTerm.description: Test earnings, transferability, and operating dependencies with a 112-item diligence checklist that connects findings to deal consequences.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Synergies
hasDefinedTerm.description: Turn synergy claims into risk-adjusted cash benefits, separate buyer-created value, and assign the operating work required to deliver it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Integration
hasDefinedTerm.description: Protect business continuity, assign operating decisions, and track acquisition value with a 104-action post-deal integration checklist.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Divestitures & carve-outs
hasDefinedTerm.description: Define what transfers, expose seller dependencies, and plan the path from Day 1 continuity to independent operations.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Strategic finance
hasDefinedTerm.description: Compare buying with alternatives, test liquidity and downside constraints, and set a private acquisition price ceiling.

item.name: Mandate
item.description: Why acquire instead of build, partner, or do nothing?
item.teaches: A defined business need, capital envelope, risk limits, executive sponsor, and decision authority.

item.name: Thesis & Targets
item.description: What must be true, and which targets fit and can actually be bought?
item.teaches: Thesis conditions, ranked target screen, pass rationale, ownership map, control path, and initial downside test.

item.name: First Look & Underwriting
item.description: Do access, standalone economics, financing, and downside support a bid?
item.teaches: Minimum information package, reconstructed financials, valuation range, financing case, and private price ceiling.

item.name: LOI & Diligence
item.description: Are core terms clear, and can the team test the conditions behind the thesis?
item.teaches: Approved LOI, evidence requests, workflow tests, accountable workstream owners, and a live issue log.
item.educationalLevel: Gates 5–6 · Exclusivity approved and diligence launched

item.name: Re-underwrite & Sign
item.description: Does the deal still work on the facts and terms now in front of the buyer?
item.teaches: Revised valuation and synergy case, combined downside, final economics, protections, closing conditions, and integration owners.

item.name: Close & Day 1
item.description: Can funds and control transfer while the business keeps working?
item.teaches: Funds flow, required consents and clearances, closing checklist, and customer, cash, people, and system readiness.
item.educationalLevel: Gates 9–10 · Closing approved and Day 1 stable

item.name: Value Delivery & Review
item.description: Has the buyer delivered the underwritten value, and what should change next time?
item.teaches: 30/60/100-day reviews, realized cash benefits and costs, workflow decisions, revised forecasts, and residual action owners.
item.educationalLevel: Gates 11–12 · Value delivery confirmed and program closed

@graph.name: Acquisition Target Pipeline & Deal Funnel
@graph.description: Manage acquisition targets from thesis through close with explicit next decisions, seller and control signals, evidence quality, private price discipline, and a durable pass-and-reopen record.
@graph.teaches: Where should the Corp Dev team spend its next increment of attention, and what must happen before each target advances?

@graph.name: M&A Investment Committee Memo: From Analysis to Approval
@graph.description: Turn mandate, valuation, diligence, deal structure, synergies, affordability, downside, and integration into one decision-ready M&A approval memo—with a worked NVIDIA–Hugging Face example.
@graph.teaches: Should the buyer make the next commitment of capital, time, exclusivity, reputation, or operating risk—and under what conditions?

@graph.name: Public Company Comps Workbench
@graph.description: Build a reviewed peer valuation with a reusable Excel template and populated Capital IQ reference comps covering 254 companies across 12 sectors.
@graph.teaches: Which public companies are genuinely comparable, and what valuation range does the reviewed peer evidence support?

@graph.name: Capital Allocation & Deal Affordability Tool
@graph.description: Compare buying, building, partnering, and doing nothing; test funding and downside constraints; and set the buyer's private hard price ceiling.
@graph.teaches: Is the acquisition the best use of capital, and what is the buyer's hard price ceiling?

@graph.name: Carve-Out Perimeter & TSA Planner
@graph.description: Define what transfers, map seller dependencies, plan temporary services and their exit, and separate Day 1 readiness from independent operations.
@graph.teaches: What is being sold, what remains entangled, and how will the business operate independently?

@graph.name: Acquisition Mandate & Target Screen
@graph.description: Decide why to acquire, compare the alternatives, and prioritize targets against clear requirements, evidence, and a credible path to ownership.
@graph.teaches: Why buy instead of build, partner, or do nothing—and which targets satisfy the mandate?

@graph.name: LOI Economics & Risk Allocator
@graph.description: See how cash, stock, rollover, deferred payments, and closing conditions change the price, funding need, and risk of a deal.
@graph.teaches: How does the proposed structure change economics, control, and risk?

@graph.name: Synergy Underwriting & Value Bridge
@graph.description: Turn synergy claims into risk-adjusted cash value, an explicit seller-sharing decision, and an operating delivery plan.
@graph.teaches: What value can the buyer create, what will it cost, and how much—if any—should be reflected in the purchase price?

@graph.name: The M&A Deal Workflow: From Mandate to Value
@graph.description: A 156-action, 13-gate buyer-side checklist from acquisition mandate through post-close review.
@graph.teaches: What must happen—and who must decide—before the buyer commits more capital, time, or operating risk?

@graph.name: NVIDIA: valuing an AI infrastructure business
@graph.description: Connect demand for computing to product economics, supply commitments, and the cash that growth can produce.
@graph.teaches: What must remain true about demand, margins, and cash conversion for the valuation to hold?

@graph.name: Surgery Partners: valuing a healthcare-services business
@graph.description: Follow cases, reimbursement, and facility ownership through to the cash the parent company can actually keep.
@graph.teaches: What cash belongs to the buyer after operating needs, partner interests, and debt are taken into account?

@graph.name: Ziff Davis: valuing a digital media business
@graph.description: Look past the audience headline to repeatable revenue, platform dependence, and the businesses actually being valued.
@graph.teaches: Which earnings can the current portfolio keep producing, and what makes those earnings vulnerable?

@graph.name: Salesforce: valuing a software business
@graph.description: Connect recurring revenue to the cost of keeping customers, delivering the service, and funding growth.
@graph.teaches: How much growth can the business turn into cash for each share after the costs of delivering it?

@graph.name: Gap: valuing a retail business
@graph.description: Start with what customers buy, what the retailer keeps, and how much cash sits in inventory.
@graph.teaches: Does the valuation hold if sales soften and the business has to discount more stock?

@graph.name: After the Deal: Keep the Business Working
@graph.description: A 104-action post-deal integration checklist and practical guide for protecting revenue, maintaining Day 1 continuity, and realizing synergies.
@graph.teaches: What must keep working, what should change, and who is responsible for the handover?

@graph.name: Before You Buy: Follow the Work
@graph.description: A 112-item M&A due diligence checklist and practical guide for testing earnings quality, workflows, dependencies, transferability, and deal consequences.
@graph.teaches: Can the business keep producing its results when the owner changes?

@graph.name: Exit readiness checklist
@graph.description: An existing seller-preparation checklist, organized around what buyers will examine.
@graph.teaches: What should an owner prepare before a buyer begins diligence?

@graph.name: Long Beach Outpatient Surgery
@graph.description: A controlling investment and the operating work behind a multi-specialty expansion.
@graph.teaches: What operating changes are required to deliver the acquisition thesis?

@graph.name: Sourcing Journal
@graph.description: Founder clarity, partner alignment, and the timing of a capability acquisition.
@graph.teaches: How do seller alignment and timing affect the transaction?

@graph.name: BuzzAngle Music
@graph.description: A strategic investment in music data, viewed through competitive position and capability.
@graph.teaches: When is a target worth more as a strategic capability than as a standalone business?

@graph.name: The five decision frames
@graph.description: Judgment, dependency, timing, signal, and scarcity: the frames behind consequential decisions.
@graph.teaches: Which frame clarifies the decision before analysis begins?

@graph.name: Business valuation scenarios
@graph.description: Explore the existing Exit Desk calculator and its indicative positioning scenarios.
@graph.teaches: How might buyer context and preparation affect an indicative valuation?
